Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant life change you've just experienced, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation, I'd like to use the EPDS, which is a helpful tool for us to understand how you're feeling during this postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us get a better sense of your emotional well-being right now.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. This assessment is not about judging or labeling; it's about understanding your unique experience and providing you with the best possible support.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and we'll go through them together. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Your responses will help me get a better understanding of your postpartum experience.

Let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to?

(sighing slightly) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same. I don't feel like I'm enjoying things as much as I did before I had the baby. Even things that used to make me really happy, like watching my favorite TV show or reading a book, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and it's hard to find the energy to laugh or have fun. (pausing, looking down) It's like, I know I should be happy, I just had a baby, but... (trailing off, struggling to find the words) ...it's just not feeling that way right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking my head slightly) No, not really. Like I said, I don't feel like I'm laughing as much as I used to. I mean, sometimes my baby will do something silly and I'll smile, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. Most of the time, I'm just worried about taking care of the baby and making sure everything is okay. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) It's hard to explain, but it feels like there's this weight on me all the time, and it's hard to shake it off and just enjoy things like I used to. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I don't know, maybe I'm just tired all the time, but it feels like more than that.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not as much as I used to. To be honest, most days I just feel like I'm trying to get through the day, you know? I don't really have the energy to think about things I'm looking forward to, or to get excited about them. Even things that I used to love, like spending time with my partner or going for a walk, just feel like another thing to add to my to-do list. (sighing) I feel like I'm just trying to survive right now, rather than really living. And when I do think about things I used to enjoy, it just makes me feel guilty because I'm not enjoying them as much as I used to. (looking down, my voice cracking slightly) It's like, I feel like I'm missing out on all the things that are supposed to be happy and fun about having a new baby.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always wondering if I'm doing something wrong, or if I'm not doing enough for the baby. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not feeding her right, or if she's not sleeping, it's because I'm not creating the right environment. (sighing) I feel like I'm constantly second-guessing myself, and it's exhausting. I'll be sitting there, feeling like I'm doing okay, and then something will happen and I'll just start thinking about all the things I could be doing better. (shaking my head) It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not good enough. (pausing, looking up) And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I feel like I'm failing as a mother, and as a partner, and as a person. (my voice cracking slightly) It's just really hard to deal with all these feelings of guilt and inadequacy.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yeah. That's me all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much? Is she too hot or too cold? (laughing nervously) I mean, it's ridiculous, because I know I'm doing my best, but I just can't seem to shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I worry about my relationship with my partner, I worry about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and the house and everything else... (trailing off) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to get rid of. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all the terrible things that could happen. Like, what if the baby gets sick? What if I'm not doing something right and it hurts her? (shaking my head) It's just this never-ending cycle of worry and fear, and it's exhausting. (taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to explain.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (taking a deep breath) It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Other times, it's when I'm trying to fall asleep, and my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios. (shaking my head) It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just can't seem to calm myself down. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) And sometimes, I'll have these thoughts... like, what if I'm not a good enough mother? What if I hurt the baby somehow? (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's just really hard to deal with, because it feels like my mind is playing tricks on me. (looking up, tears in my eyes) I just feel so overwhelmed and scared all the time.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yeah, that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to be a good partner... it all just feels so overwhelming. (sighing) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start feeling like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities. (looking down, my voice cracking) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. (shaking my head) I don't know how to explain it, but it's like... everything just feels too much for me to handle right now. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to do all of this. I should be able to take care of the baby, and be a good partner, and keep the house clean... but it's just not happening. (looking up, tears in my eyes) I feel like I'm failing, and it's really hard to deal with.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Oh, yeah. That's me. I've been having a really hard time sleeping. I'll lie awake at night, thinking about everything that's going on, and just feeling really overwhelmed. (sighing) It's like, my mind won't turn off, and I just can't seem to relax. I'll be thinking about the baby, and worrying about whether I'm doing everything right, and just feeling really anxious. (shaking my head) And even when I do fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and just lie there, feeling really unhappy and worried. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) It's like, I'll be thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and just feeling really scared and alone. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And it's hard, because I know I need sleep to take care of the baby, but it's just not happening. (looking up, tears in my eyes) I feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of unhappiness and anxiety, and I don't know how to get out of it. (my voice cracking) Some nights, I'll wake up, and just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes, that's me. I've been feeling really sad and miserable a lot of the time. It's like, I'll be going about my day, taking care of the baby, and just doing everything I'm supposed to do, but inside, I'm just feeling really empty and unhappy. (sighing) I'll be looking at the baby, and she'll be smiling at me, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'm supposed to be happy, I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby, but instead, I just feel really down. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be doing laundry, or making dinner, and just feeling really overwhelmed and sad. (shaking my head) I don't know, it's just like, I'm stuck in this cloud of sadness, and I don't know how to get out of it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and just feeling really hopeless. Like, I don't know how I'm going to get through this, or how I'm going to be a good mother. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's just really hard, and I feel really alone. (my voice cracking) I've even had thoughts, like, what's the point of all of this? Why am I even doing this? (quickly covering my mouth, as if I've said something I shouldn't have) I'm sorry, I don't know why I said that. It's just... it's just really hard right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that I'm not alone) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. (wiping away tears) It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed and unhappy, and I don't know how to deal with it. (sighing) I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and just start crying. It's like, I'm just so tired, and so stressed, and so anxious, and it all just becomes too much. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) I've even cried in front of my partner, which is really hard for me. I don't like showing weakness, but it's just... it's just really hard right now. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've cried about everything, from the baby not sleeping, to feeling like I'm not a good enough mother, to just feeling really overwhelmed and alone. (looking up, tears streaming down my face) It's just... it's just really hard, and I don't know how to make it stop. (sobbing) I feel like I'm just crying all the time, and I don't know how to be happy again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(looking down, feeling a sense of shame and embarrassment) Yeah... I don't know how to talk about this, but... (pausing, taking a deep breath) Yes, those thoughts have occurred to me. (my voice is barely above a whisper) It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeling really overwhelmed and sad, and suddenly I'll just have this thought... like, what if I just didn't exist anymore? Or, what if I just did something to hurt myself? (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's like, I know it's not rational, and I know it's not something I would ever actually do, but... (shaking my head) It's just, sometimes it feels like the pain and the sadness are just too much to bear, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've had these thoughts a few times, and it's always when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and alone. (looking down, my voice cracking) I feel like I'm a bad person for even thinking those thoughts, and I don't know how to deal with them. (sobbing) I just feel like I'm losing myself, and I don't know how to find my way back. (looking up, pleadingly) Please, you have to promise not to judge me, or think I'm a bad person. I just need help, and I don't know where else to turn.

They report difficulty coping with the demands of caring for a new baby and experience anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient indicates they don't laugh as much as they used to and have a hard time feeling carefree, matching 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a significant decrease in looking forward to things, using phrases like 'Not as much as I used to' and 'I don't really have the energy to think about things I'm looking forward to', which aligns with the option 'Definitely less than I used to</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports being anxious or worried 'all the time' and describes a constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that is exhausting, indicating a high frequency of anxiety.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense feelings of panic and anxiety, often triggered by thoughts of being a good mother or worst-case scenarios, indicating a high level of distress.</sym>, <sym>Patient expresses feeling overwhelmed by responsibilities, barely holding it together, and feeling like they're drowning in tasks, indicating a strong sense of not being able to cope.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have been feeling sad and miserable a lot of the time, describing feelings of emptiness, unhappiness, and overwhelm, even when doing everyday tasks or interacting with their baby.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>The patient reports having thoughts of self-harm, describing them as occurring 'a few times' when feeling 'really overwhelmed and alone', which aligns with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and EPDS score indicate a high level of emotional distress and difficulty coping with the demands of caring for a new baby. The presence of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and feelings of guilt and worthlessness, combined with anxiety and sleep difficulties, suggests a probable diagnosis of <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's report of self-harm thoughts is a significant safety concern that requires immediate attention and follow-up. This screening impression is based on the EPDS guidelines and <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if experiencing suicidal thoughts
3. Develop a safety plan with the patient to ensure their safety and well-being
4. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum depression</med> support and treatment
5. Schedule follow-up appointment to monitor patient's symptoms and adjust treatment plan as needed
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
